newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies close lower, Swiss francs fall.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies close lower, Swiss francs fall.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures closed lower, with Swiss francs leading declines as the U.S. dollar overall benefitted from the strong rally in the U.S. bond and stock markets, traders and analysts said.
December Swiss francs fell below the two-month low at $0.8136, as the dollar/Swiss franc closed higher for the seventh session in a row, one technical analyst said.

The $0.8136 level is roughly equivalent to the 1.2400 spot Swiss franc level and represents a 62-percent retracement level of the dollar/Swiss franc's decline, he said. December Swiss francs set a session low of $0.8104.
December marks remained above $0.6637, as the dollar/mark failed to test the 62-percent retracement level during U.S. hours.

Swiss franc futures gained downward momentum, as marks flirted with slim losses, due to the cash mark/Swiss franc rate. The rate, spurred by the Swiss National Bank's liquidity injections in early trade, rose through 81.85, a 20-month moving average, technical analysts said.
Dave Durrant, a senior currency anlayst at I.D.E.A., Inc added that dealers, who sold high-yielding currencies against Swiss francs, were unwinding those positions.
The attraction to the high-yielding currencies is based on underlying concerns about European Monetary Union (EMU) talks, several analysts said. They are now focusing on EMU talks in Dublin.
"The dollar would have been stronger against the mark if it weren't for mark/yen," Durrant said. The cash mark/yen rebounded near the 73.00 level.

One technician said mark/yen could fill a gap at 73.25 to 73.30, but that the rate would have difficulty puncturing a technical level at 73.67. December yen, meanwhile, set a contract low at $0.009162.

Earlier in the day, December yen rebounded off its initial low set in reaction to the modest gains in the U.S. August Consumer Price Index (CPI) and retail sales data. The tepid month-to-month rises in consumer prices and sales erased expectations for a U.S. interest rate hike in September.
"I think interest rate differentials matter, but probably not at this level for the dollar," one cash forex trader said, adding that institutions were buying dollars and U.S. assets.
Canadian dollar futures were higher, benefiting from the gains in U.S.-dollar denominated assets. December Canadian dollars came within a hair of resistance at $0.7336.
The $0.7336 level corresponds to a spot rate of 1.3685 spot. Further resistance is at $0.7345, or 1.3668 spot, one trader said.

At the end of pit trade, December yen were off $0.000020 at $0.009169, marks down $0.0002 at $0.6647, Swiss francs off $0.0033 at $0.8115, sterling up $0.0006 at $1.5546, Canadian dollars were up $0.0010 at $0.7331 and Austalian dollars were down $0.0060 at $0.7883.
